title: Map pins, camera filters, and profile updates

recentMessages.text:
Committed. Nothing else is pending.

**Commit** 89d260b on clay-map main, 51 files: the camera rail shortcuts, the ClayWheel bow flip and wider feed column, the profile and opened-post map button with its Home-to-Map handoff, the location relay into the map iframe, the 16 AR thumbnails, the 14 channel icons, the three new side icons at all three sizes, and the manifest and test-count updates.

**What stayed out, on purpose.** Another session staged its own work into the shared index while I was preparing this (FeedTwin, pinSpread, MapBootCover, the 17 feed photos, and its own hunks in HomeTwin and MapApp). I built the commit from a private index so none of that came along, and their staging is still intact for them to commit. The peer's later edit to the feed dial's vertical order is also theirs and remains uncommitted.

**Not committed anywhere:** the synced bundles in the iOS, Android, and React Native repos. The phone's installed build came from that iOS working tree, so if you want the release checkpoint recorded, the usual "sync the clay-map bundle at 89d260b" commits in those three repos are the next step. Nothing has been pushed.
commit
Committing the synced bundles in the three native repos. Checking each repo's state first so only the bundle paths go in, and re-verifying the bundle content before recording it.

All four commits are in, and every repo's bundle path is clean against its new HEAD (the "dirty" entries after committing were only the shared index lagging behind the moved HEAD, now realigned; no newer peer sync had landed).

- **clay-map** 89d260b: source, icons, and tests (51 files).
- **iOS** 7b022b5 and **Android** be544b1: the synced bundle from the 17:04 build, identical trees, carrying the Kodak/camcorder rail, the profile map button, the dial bow, the location relay, the new AR thumbnails, and the manifest pointing the channels pack at the published digest 66c00f2d76ac.
- **React Native** 4d7381b: the bundle marker for the matching 17:13 zip.

Each commit was built from a private index so peer sessions' staged work stayed untouched. The bundle predates the clay-map commit by about ninety minutes but contains the same changes, and its message says so. Nothing has been pushed to any remote.
push to connected iphone
Installing the committed state on the iPhone. Checking the machine is free of other builds, then dispatching the build runner against the iOS tree at 7b022b5.

The iPhone build is running from the committed tree (7b022b5, bundle chunk index-DkqlwDuh.js, channels digest 66c00f2d76ac). Nothing else to do until the install result comes back; I'll report as soon as it does.

Installed. The iPhone now runs the committed state.

- **Build** ios-iphone-20260902-192355 from the iOS tree at 7b022b5, no errors, installed at 19:31 without an uninstall, so your permissions are intact.
- **Bundle verified inside the .app**: main chunk index-DkqlwDuh.js and the manifest's channels digest 66c00f2d76ac, both byte-identical to the committed copies. This replaces the earlier install, which still carried the previous chunk.

That bundle includes everything from today: the Kodak/camcorder shortcuts, the flipped dials with the new AR and channel art, the profile map button, the location relay for the map's reach test, and the peer sessions' AR filter parts. Nothing has been pushed to any remote.
this is still not right. the ui should be matching the ui of the uploading pipeline, and aligned correctly

I see it: the photo review is drawn over the live camera chrome, so the rail, the AR dial, the zoom presets and the channel arrows all bleed through around it, and the frame sits offset with the label colliding with the logo. Let me find the review screen and the upload-pipeline UI it should match.
Writing the rebuilt review on the composer's stage, preview, chrome chip, panel and button classes, with a small module of its own for the two-button row.
The test passes now. The headless cube tap didn't open the review, so I'm checking what state the camera ended in and whether the upload-flow harness can render the review stage directly.

Committed the review fix as 01a7046. A peer session is also running a bundle sync right now, so mine may hit the thermal gate under contention; I'll check its result when it reports and rerun if needed, then build and install.
The sync passed and the phone bundle now carries the review fix (chunk index-D1hUHJ9r.js, channels digest intact). Dispatching the iPhone build; it will wait out any peer xcodebuild first.
The iPhone build is queued behind any peer build and running. Once it installs, I'll commit the three native bundle syncs to match what shipped and report.
commit
Committing the three native bundle syncs now. Checking the trees first so the commit records exactly what is there.
The React Native commit failed only because that command ran from the wrong directory (the shell reset its cwd and I omitted the cd). Nothing was written; redoing it in the RN repo.

Committed in all three native repos, each from a private index so peer sessions' staging stayed untouched:

- **iOS** e9945478 and **Android** 724bc1f: the synced bundle (identical trees, chunk index-BsxGDAIs.js) carrying the capture review on the composer's stage, on top of the peers' Analytics commits. Channels digest still 66c00f2d76ac.
- **React Native** 696482e: the bundle marker for the matching zip.
- **clay-map** 01a7046 was already in from before.

The iPhone build from that tree is still running; I'll report the install result when it lands. Nothing has been pushed to any remote.
